title: An oasis on the Silk Road preserves 4,000 years of history
body: The ruins of ancient Merv in Turkmenistan cover a large oasis. People settled there across some four millennia, leaving monuments from successive periods rather than one single city plan.
takeaway: A dependable source of water can keep drawing settlements back to the same area even as cities rise and fall.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Ancient Merv (1999)
visual: earthen ruins on the edge of a green oasis surrounded by desert

title: Timbuktu was a centre of learning in the 15th and 16th centuries
body: Timbuktu in present-day Mali was home to Sankore and other Islamic schools. The city's three great mosques, Sankore, Djingareyber and Sidi Yahia, are surviving landmarks of that period.
takeaway: The buildings mark a place where scholarship and religious life were closely connected.
visual: the earthen walls and wooden projections of Sankore Mosque
